onset_definition.threshold_basis: strictly above the familiar per-task CPU clip (1860) and below the registered burst floor (4400): only a cascade burst can cross it
onset_definition.new_event_rule: the previous interval must not already be inside the same burst, and creation_id must exist at both t-1 and t
onset_definition.source: task's own demand only, never the host aggregate

matched_controls.M0: marginal-matched lag-shuffled: keep every task's marginal amplitude, duration distribution and RAM/Disk windows, but re-pair the windows with a uniformly drawn lag (registered lags destroyed)
matched_controls.M1: order-shuffled: keep the same resource events but reveal them in a randomly permuted temporal order
matched_controls.M2: within-task circular shift: circularly shift each task's RAM/Disk deviation trajectory, preserving marginals and autocorrelation but destroying the registered causal alignment

mechanism.physics_note: controlled unseen temporal resource-demand regime; the two-stage CPU phase is required by Simulator.getPlacementPossible() evaluating demand at the admission interval (P21-01), not a claim about real industrial fault laws
